assertions.name: q0_does_not_cancel_in_lepton_ratio
assertions.source: m_μ/m_e ratio residual equals the mass residual because m_e is the q_0-independent CAL-1 anchor; the q_0 lever survives.

description: EXPLORATORY feasibility probe (PR #1753): bare-categorical m_μ residual, q_0 non-cancellation in m_μ/m_e, sensitivity lever, and one torus-tower candidate level. NO CODATA fit; audit-only.

data.structural_note: Muon canonical knot 4_1 is hyperbolic, NOT a torus knot. T(2,k) torus knots (3_1,5_1,7_1) have Vol=0, so a literal torus tower cannot reuse the Vol(4_1)/ℏ_q² lever. Reducing the 209.8 ppb requires a NON-Vol invariant or accepting the q_0-driven floor (211 ppb tracks the q_0 re-pin shift, H1).
data.feasibility_verdict: The 209.8 ppb bare-categorical residual is H1-confirmed as the q_0 re-pin shift (-11.6 ppb) amplified ~18x by the Vol(4_1)/ℏ_q² lever. m_e (CAL-1) is q_0-independent, so q_0 does NOT cancel in m_μ/m_e. The single-term S=0 formula has no shell to add a PROVED categorical correction to without a new invariant. Reducing below ~211 ppb is therefore q_0-limited (Subgoal-2, owner-declined) UNLESS a new lepton-tower categorical term (non-Vol) is derived that shifts the prediction toward CODATA WITHOUT being a fit.
